newsitem.title: USA: US PLAINS FED CATTLE BID $64.00, PASSED - FEEDLOTS.
newsitem.headline: US PLAINS FED CATTLE BID $64.00, PASSED - FEEDLOTS.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade was locked in a stalemate, with packer bids at $64.00 per cwt passed by cattle owners asking $65.00, feedlot sources said.

"We had two buyers (Wednesday) that paid $65.00 early and then they all went to bid $64.00 and that stopped the trading," a Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma feedlot manager said. "Nobody's going to sell cattle today at $64.00, so we'll wait until Monday," he said.
However, if no cattle sell Thursday there will be a large number carried over onto showlists next week, sources said.
Cattle owners were fighting a price slide to $64.00 because it would wipe out the small profits that some cattle feeder were making at $65.00, sources said.
Fed cattle prices this week were pressured by sharp declines in beef values as packers discounted prices vigorously to move supplies, they said.
Beef prices on Wednesday were quoted $1.33 to $1.73 per cwt lower, with 350 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported.
Heavyweight choice beef was quoted at $105.92, down $1.49 from Tuesday and down $2.95 from Friday, USDA statistics showed.
